page.title: The missing harbour bell
page.description: A storm, a silent bell, and a ferry due at dusk. A short fictional mystery: what you investigate changes what you can do.

scenes.heading: An empty hook
scenes.text:
At six, you pull the harbour bell's rope. Nothing. The bronze bell is gone. Its fastening lies neatly on the wall, streaked with blue grease.

The ferry will arrive before dark. Without the bell, its captain won't know the inner harbour is safe. You can raise the red closure flag now, or spend the remaining daylight finding out what happened.

choices.label: Follow the grease to the repair shed
Raise the closure flag; don't risk the arrival

scenes.heading: A repair interrupted
scenes.text:
The shed is empty. On the workbench: a broken sluice latch, a fresh wooden brace, and a note in Mara's square handwriting: NEED WEIGHT TO HOLD GATE OPEN.

A rope drags a blue line toward the drainage channel. This looks less like theft than a repair gone wrong. You can carry the brace there, but it will take the last few minutes of daylight.

choices.label: Take the brace to the drainage channel
Stop investigating and close the harbour

scenes.heading: Both hands on the rope
scenes.text:
You find Mara by the sluice, holding a rope against her shoulder. The bell hangs at its other end as a counterweight, keeping the drainage gate open.

‘The latch snapped. If I let go before it's braced, the lower workshops flood.’ Her blue gloves slip. ‘There's a brace in my shed. Or take my signal lamp to the outer pier and guide the ferry there. I can't do both.’

choices.label: Fetch the brace and help Mara restore the bell
Take the lamp; keep the ferry outside
Close the harbour and stay to hold the rope

scenes.heading: Not a thief. A missing pair of hands.
scenes.text:
You bring the brace to the sluice. Mara points to the safe slot beside the broken latch. Together you secure the gate, ease the load off the rope, and lift the bell free.

By the time you rehang it, the ferry's bow light is rounding the point. One clear note crosses the water. The workshops stay dry; the ferry reaches its usual berth. Tomorrow's notice asks for a second person on storm duty — not a suspect's name.

scenes.heading: A different landing
scenes.text:
You carry Mara's lamp to the outer pier and signal the ferry to stop there. Its captain spots you. The passengers arrive safely, though they must walk the long seawall in the rain.

The captain sends two deckhands back with you. They relieve Mara and brace the sluice. The bell stays silent until morning, but no one mistakes silence for safety tonight.

scenes.heading: Company at the sluice
scenes.text:
You raise the red flag, then return to share the rope's weight. The ferry turns toward the next harbour. Mara's shoulders finally drop.

With you holding the gate, she fetches the brace. The workshops are saved. Passengers arrive by bus much later, annoyed but safe. On the incident form you write: one person was asked to keep two things running.

scenes.heading: A safe delay, an unanswered question
scenes.text:
The red flag goes up. The ferry diverts before the light fails. You cannot promise a safe entrance, so you don't.

Later, Mara explains why she borrowed the bell: a broken sluice latch, a gate that needed a counterweight, no spare hands. She managed to secure it, but water reached the lowest workshop. Nobody was hurt. The harbour was safe; the mystery could have used another minute of your attention.

props.label: How do the choices matter?
props.text: Following the evidence can restore the bell. Speaking to Mara opens two other ways to help. Closing immediately avoids risking the ferry but leaves you without the full explanation until later. There are four endings; Back and Start over let you explore them. No timer is running.

reply: A ready-made mystery with four endings. Investigate the missing bell, help the mechanic, or put safety first. The choices change what gets resolved. There is no real countdown; use Back or Start over to explore another path.
